'''Charles William Hellaby''' is a South African mathematician who is an associate professor of [[applied mathematics]] at the [[University of Cape Town]], [[South Africa]], working in the field of [[cosmology]].<ref name="UCTStaff"/> He is a member of the [[International Astronomical Union]]<ref name="IAU 2017"/> and a member of the [[Baháʼí Faith]].<ref name="UCTFaith"/>

== Life ==
Hellaby was born to Rev. William Allen Meldrum Hellaby and Emily Madeline Hellaby. His twin brother, Mark Edwin Hellaby, pursued a career in literature while his younger brother, Julian Meldrum Hellaby, took to music as a career.<ref name="Telegraph 2010"/> He obtained a BSc (Physics & Astronomy) at the [[University of St Andrews]], [[Scotland]] in 1977. He completed his MSc ([[Theory of Relativity|Relativity]]) at [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]], [[Kingston, Ontario]] in 1981 and his PhD (Relativity) at Queen's University in 1985.<ref name="UCTStaff"/>

From 1985 to 1988 he was a Post Doctoral Researcher at the [[University of Cape Town]] under [[George F. R. Ellis|George Ellis]]. In 1989 he was appointed a lecturer at the University of Cape Town.<ref name="UCTStaff"/><ref name="QU"/>

Hellaby is a member of the [[International Astronomical Union]] (Division J Galaxies and Cosmology), having previously been a member of Division VIII Galaxies & the Universe and subsequently Commission 47 Cosmology.<ref name="IAU 2017"/>

== Research ==
His research interests include:

* [[Inhomogeneous cosmology]].  Standard cosmology assumes a [[cosmological principle|smooth homogeneous universe]], but the real universe is very lumpy
* Inhomogeneous cosmological models - their evolution, geometry and [[Gravitational singularity|singularities]]
* Non-linear structure formation in the universe
* Extracting the geometry of the cosmos from observations
* The [[Georges Lemaître|Lemaitre]]&ndash;[[Richard C. Tolman|Tolman]] cosmological model
* The [[Peter Szekeres|Szekeres]] cosmological model
* Junction conditions in GR
* Dense [[black holes]]
* Local inhomogeneities and the Swiss cheese model

He has also worked on
* The models of [[P. C. Vaidya|Vaidya]], [[Schwarzschild metric|Schwarzschild]]&ndash;[[Kruskal–Szekeres coordinates|Kruskal–Szekeres]] & [[William Morris Kinnersley|Kinnersley]]
* Classical signature change
* Cosmic strings
* Gravitational collapse

Hellaby co-authored ''Structures in the Universe by Exact Methods: Formation, Evolution, Interactions''<ref name="Structures"/> in which applications of inhomogenous solutions to [[Albert Einstein]]'s field equations of cosmology are reviewed. The structure of galaxy clusters, galaxies with central [[black hole]]s and [[supernova]]e dimming can be studied with the aid of inhomogenous models.<ref name="QU"/>
